title: Corrected Theorem A / A' (interpolation and algebraic-SLP lower bounds)
question:
Theorem A (corrected, generalized): Let E/F_p be short Weierstrass and P in E(F_p) of order r >= 3 (no condition r != p). If a rational function f on E is defined at kP and satisfies f(kP) = k mod p for 1 <= k <= N <= r-1, then deg(f) (pole divisor degree) >= (N-1)/2, and a polynomial f in X, Y has total degree >= (N-1)/6. Proof: h = f∘τ_P − f − 1 has the N−1 distinct zeros kP (1 <= k <= N−1) and deg h <= 2 deg f; if h ≡ 0 then the pole set of f is invariant under translation by P, so it is a union of

-orbits of size r, giving deg f >= r > (N−1)/2 (f is nonconstant since f(P) != f(2P) when N >= 2). Theorem A' (corrected constant, explicit model): in the algebraic SLP model over F_q with +, −, ×, ÷ where every division is defined at every kP (no comparisons, no x/0 convention), computing k mod p for all kP, 1 <= k <= N, requires length >= log2((N−1)/6). The Ω(n^2) bit-cost statement holds only under the extra charge of Ω(log q) bit operations per field operation; it is not a bit-complexity lower bound for ECDLP.
rationale: Corrected variant from blind adversarial review ECDLP-17; original HYP-5a550ab6 kept with its flawed proof step recorded.

notes: Reviewer: adversarial-critic (Sonnet, configured); PI checked the p|r example (p=5, E: y^2=x^3+3x, P=(2,2) of order 10) with the toy oracle. Rational interpolants with deg ~ (N+1)/2 exist, so the constant 1/2 is nearly sharp for rational f. Novelty not found / not settled. | ECDLP-22 novelty: Lange–Winterhof (COCOON 2002, LNCS 2387, pp. 137–143) prove degree lower bounds for interpolating the EC discrete logarithm, refined by Satoh (WCC 2005, LNCS 3969): Theorem A is KNOWN IN KIND; exact comparison of constants not possible (full texts not accessed). Do not claim novelty.
